extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of poetry and drama (playwrights, critics, literature students)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and evaluating classical dramatic poetry (tragedy, comedy, epic/romance) following Aristotle’s Poetics: definitions, essential elements (plot, character, diction/thought, music, spectacle), meter selection, and the emotional aims (pity, fear, catharsis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: A Tragedy is ... the portrayal of an imaginary chapter of heroic life, complete and of some length, in language sweetened in different parts in all known ways, in dramatic, not narrative form, indirectly through pity and terror righting mental disorders of this type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tragedy should present an imagined episode (a 'fictitious chapter of life') in enacted/dramatic form (not mere narration). Language and other devices should 'sweeten' portions of the work; the dramatic action must evoke pity and fear so as to effect a corrective/cathartic outcome for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six Factors of Tragedy
rubrics_metrics.description: A Tragedy must thus have six Factors, analytically speaking: Story, Psychology, Diction, Intelligence, Presentation, Music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the elemental dimensions by which a tragedy is constituted and should be evaluated: Story (plot) and Psychology (character/intellect) concern the theme; Diction, Presentation (spectacle), and Music form the clothing; two factors apply to the clothing, one to treatment, three to the theme. Every dramatis persona embodies these factors in corresponding ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of Plot (Story)
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important of these is the group of occurrences; for Tragedy portrays not imaginary human beings, but an experience, a condition of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot (the sequence/group of events) is the central component of tragic art; the story (the 'group of occurrences') determines the work’s quality more than individual character details. The plot should be a coherent, complete episode (having a beginning, middle, end).

rubrics_metrics.name: Character and Intellect requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Since it is an imaginary experience, lived by individuals of the genus 'conscious and responsible beings' ... we get two causes, character and intellect, for the fictitious conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatic persons must be credible, conscious, responsible agents whose conduct derives from both character (disposition, moral traits) and intellect (reasoning, thought). Character is shown in speech and action; intellect is manifested in verbal demonstrations and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction / 'Sweetened' Language
rubrics_metrics.description: By 'sweetened language' I mean that which has Rhythm, mixture with the unfamiliar, and Tune; by 'in different parts in all known ways' that only certain parts are restrained by metres and others again by tune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language should be ornamented selectively by (1) rhythm/periodic recurrence, (2) 'harmony' (mixture of familiar and foreign diction), and (3) musical tune where appropriate. Different segments of the drama may use different verbal restraints; metre and musical tuning are distinct devices and are not necessarily applied simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music as a Dramatic Factor
rubrics_metrics.description: By musical composition a thing whose whole force is on the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Music functions as a surface, direct appeal (a universal language) that sweetens parts of the performance. It is one of the essential 'clothing' components and should be composed to enhance the dramatic illusion and emotional effect rather than to convey hidden interpretive layers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation / Spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the dramatis personae go through their parts themselves, one factor of a Tragedy must necessarily be presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staging, gesture, masks, scenery and visual elements constitute presentation. Although often less 'essential' than plot or character, presentation is a necessary dramatic factor and should be considered when composing or evaluating performance (how the action is physically realized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Aim: Pity, Fear, and Catharsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirectly through pity and terror righting mental disorders of this type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tragedy aims to arouse pity and fear in the audience and thereby produce a corrective catharsis (emotional purging or righting). Effective tragic composition intentionally elicits these emotions through plot and characterization to achieve the therapeutic/transformative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Time (Temporal Constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tragedy trying to keep within, or nearly within, a revolution of the sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classical tragic action ideally compresses the exhibited events into a short continuous time-span (roughly a day) to maintain time-illusion and unity. Longer durations are characteristic of epic/romance, which has no strict time-limit. Unity of time also has practical scenic/technical justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy is ... the portrayal of an inferior class, yet not in all their inferiority, being the ludicrous side of ugliness abstracted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comedy should present characters or a class with their ludicrous traits singled out (the 'ludicrous side' abstracted) rather than depicting their full, destructive defects. The portrayal centers on the amusing, not the painful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and Limits of the Ludicrous
rubrics_metrics.description: Ludicrousness is ... of the genus failing: the painless and non-destructive variety of the species ugliness of the genus failing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic defects should be failures or defects that do not cause genuine pain or destroy the nature of the subject (e.g., a comic foreign accent may be amusing so long as it does not make speech unintelligible). Vices used for comic effect (like drunkenness) are effective only so long as they remain non-destructive; if they evoke pain or horror they cease to be comic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate Meter Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The suitability of the iambic is presently said to be due to its resemblance to the rhythm of conversation ... the anapaest ... has the unmistakable effect of an attack ... Boccum most interestingly assigns the metres to different forms of labour; the iambus and the trochee are stamping measures ... the dactyl and anapaest are hammer-measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose metre to match the dramatic effect and the nature of actions: iambic for conversational or business-like speech, trochee as an early/dance-like foot, anapaest/dactyl for attack/hammering rhythms, spondee for striking effects. Meter can embody and reinforce the mood, tempo, and social register of a scene or character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of Tragedy to Romance/Epic
rubrics_metrics.description: Tragedy has all that Romance has, but Romance has not all that Tragedy has.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or composing Romance (epic), bear in mind that tragedy’s criteria (plot unity, enactment, time-constraint, emotional catharsis, dramatic presentation) encompass many standards applicable to epic, but epic also includes narrative freedoms (longer span, simpler metre, absence of music) not demanded of tragedy. Critique of tragedy thus covers many aspects of epic as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masks, Chorus, and Early Performative Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the mask, the prologue and the caste the contributors are unknown ... The mask appears to go back to the early history of the performance, being a mode of rendering the actor ridiculous ... The chorus ... is found in some of the Sicilian Comedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In performance practice, consider the traditional functions of masks (character transformation, ridicule), chorus (collective voice/dance), and prologue (expository opening). These elements influence tone and audience reception and may be used deliberately to connect to ritualistic or conventional dramatic forms.
